topics.title: U.S. debt reaches $40 trillion
topics.summary: The U.S. national debt has topped $40 trillion, with interest payments now one of the federal government’s biggest costs as spending continues to outpace revenue.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio had a tab that big, who would make a spreadsheet, who would suggest coupons, and who would quietly hide the snack receipts?

topics.title: Venezuela signs U.S. oil deals
topics.summary: Venezuelan oil officials visited Houston and signed early contracts with U.S. companies, marking a new step for energy ties after Nicolás Maduro’s capture.
topics.discussionPrompt: Who would treat a surprise business visit like a diplomatic puzzle, and who would mostly want to know whether the coffee in the meeting was any good?

topics.title: Iran pressure campaign widens
topics.summary: Iran dismissed new U.S. economic threats as Washington pushed wider pressure on Tehran, while regional governments reacted to the prolonged conflict and settlement disputes.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a situation shifts from loud threats to economic pressure, who starts reading the fine print and who just asks if anyone brought snacks?

topics.title: UK youth work gap grows
topics.summary: A UK review is focusing on nearly one million young people not in work, school, or training, with attention on mental health, skills, and early support.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio had to design a better first job path, who would build a mentorship board and who would accidentally make orientation too theatrical?

topics.title: GCSE results show mixed picture
topics.summary: Students in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland received GCSE results, with girls still ahead overall, boys improving in maths, and regional grade gaps continuing.
topics.discussionPrompt: Who would overreact to one exam result, who would give surprisingly calm advice, and who would claim they invented an easier grading system?
